subject: Payment routing, min-commit phasing, and Exhibit B language
messages:
From: Jessica Clark <jessica.clark@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Payment routing & min-commit phasing — need confirmation

Karthik —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Team asked for a short note outlining how Redwood expects invoicing to flow and how the minimum commitment can be phased across Q1/Q2 in our order form. Two asks from procurement:

- Confirm invoicing entity and remit-to for US/EU invoices (we need legal names and VAT/tax handling notes).
- Can the minimum commitment be tranch(ed) across two quarterly installments instead of an upfront lump sum? If so, we need the schedule in writing for our PO and internal approval.

I've attached a draft invoice schedule and Acme PO template for reference (Acme-Invoice-Schedule-v2.xlsx). Our legal team will circulate redlines to the order form once we see the payment path.

Best,
Jessica Clark
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Corp

[Attachment: Acme-Invoice-Schedule-v2.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: Jessica Clark <jessica.clark@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Payment routing & min-commit phasing — proposed approach

Kimberly / Ben —

Forwarding Jessica's note from Acme. Short proposal from Redwood to keep procurement moving:

1) Invoicing / remit: Redwood US, Inc. (TIN: 92-XXXXXXX) will be the remit-to for USD invoices; Redwood EU SAS will issue EUR invoices to Acme Europe LTD. Tax: Redwood will list VAT where applicable; Acme to confirm whether reverse-charge applies for specific EU entities.

2) Minimum commitment phasing: We can split the initial minimum commitment into two tranches — 60% due on contract commencement / activation, 40% due at the start of the following quarter. We will add an Exhibit B payment schedule table to the order form with exact dates.

3) Net terms: Redwood standard is Net 30. Acme requested Net 45 on the call. Ben, can Finance accept Net 45 for this deal given the commit size (deal ACME-3471)?

4) PO and documentation: ask Acme for a PO number on first invoice; we will provide invoice template and line-item breakdown.

I've attached a suggested payment routing spreadsheet and a redline placeholder for Exhibit B (proposed_payment_routing.xlsx, redlines_orderform_2028-01-09.pdf). Kimberly, if legal is comfortable with Exhibit B language + the tranche schedule, I'll ask legal to prepare a narrow redline to the order form (MSA remains unchanged).

Action items:
- Ben: confirm Net 45 / cash-impact comment (CC finance ops)
- Kimberly: quick review of Exhibit B payment language and tax note for EU reverse-charge
- Jessica: confirm PO process and whether your AP needs consolidated monthly invoicing or per-tranche invoices

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: proposed_payment_routing.xlsx, redlines_orderform_2028-01-09.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Cc: Jessica Clark <jessica.clark@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jan 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment routing & min-commit phasing — proposed approach

Karthik / Kimberly —

Finance is comfortable accepting Net 45 for ACME-3471 provided the following conditions are included in the invoice workflow:

- Acme provides a PO number on the first invoice and indicates the exact remit entity per tranche.
- Any invoices outstanding beyond Net 60 will incur an administrative hold and potential service pauses (we prefer to avoid this but want the option).
- Tax withholding: if Acme's AP withholds taxes in any jurisdiction, we need to receive withhold certificates or the gross-up amount will be reconciled on the next invoice.

Kimberly: can Legal confirm whether the above can be captured in the Exhibit B payment notes (non-substantive to MSA) so Acme's team sees the conditions explicitly?

Jessica: we can proceed with Net 45 on the signed order form once legal confirms Exhibit B language.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance
Redwood Inference

[Note: internal finance approval; no external attachment]

From: Wilson & Co Legal <legal@wilsonco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: Jessica Clark <jessica.clark@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 20 Jan 2028 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: ACME-3471 — Exhibit B redline and invoice path (attached)

Kimberly / Karthik —

Attached are Acme counsel's redline comments to the Order Form Exhibit B (redlines_orderform_2028-01-09.pdf). High level: Acme accepts the tranche approach but requests:

- Explicit mapping in Exhibit B for which legal entity will issue each tranche invoice (US entity vs EU entity).
- Net 45 is acceptable from Acme's side; they ask for a 45-day calendar count from invoice date.
- Clarify VAT handling: where Acme is subject to reverse-charge, they will self-account; otherwise Redwood should charge VAT on EUR invoices.

We reviewed Finance's conditions. Acme is fine with PO on first invoice and documenting administrative hold beyond Net 60, but they asked to soften the pause language ("administrative hold" -> "suspension of services after notice and cure period"). Please confirm the final Exhibit B wording and we will push to execution and DocuSign.

Next steps we propose: Redwood finalizes Exhibit B wording (payment routing table + tax note + PO requirement) and returns a clean copy; Acme will countersign and provide PO. Once signed, Redwood to send DocuSign link for signatures.

Regards,
Alice Wilson
Wilson & Co — Outside Counsel to Acme

[Attachment: redlines_orderform_2028-01-09.pdf]
